metadata.scope: Non-merge commits reachable from the pinned ref; all parents traversed. Shallow repositories contain only locally reachable history.
metadata.identity: Git mailmap-normalized author email, case-insensitive; name fallback when email is empty. Git also reads configured and working-tree mailmaps. IDs and contributor links use an anchor commit, not a GitHub login. Identity mapping can merge or split people and IDs can change when history or mailmap changes.
metadata.paths: Tree differences from the single parent (or empty tree for roots); renames are represented as deletion and addition. Paths containing @ are omitted. Paths are decoded as UTF-8; non-UTF-8 names may be lossy.
metadata.sampling: Top contributors by full-history non-merge commit count; per-contributor commits in git date-order, selected round-robin. Files are first encountered in sampled-commit and git path order, subject to global and per-commit limits.
